It solves the memory bottleneck of explicit storage in dynamic scenes by using a compact neural function to generate deformation features at query time, reducing the memory footprint compared to prior works that rely on deep hash grid hierarchies [S1].

The claim states that the method solves the memory bottleneck of explicit storage in dynamic scenes by using a compact neural function to generate deformation features at query time, reducing memory footprint compared to prior works relying on deep hash grid hierarchies. Source [S1] explicitly supports this: 1) It states the method replaces 'learnable multi-resolution hash grids for deformation features with a compact neural function that generates features at query time' (Passage 1). 2) It mentions this serves as a 'storage-efficient counterpart' and 'eliminates the memory bottleneck of explicit storage' (Passage 3). 3) It contrasts this with prior works that rely on 'deep hierarchies (e.g., typically 16 levels)' and notes their method uses only '4 to 5 resolution levels' to optimize storage efficiency (Passage 4). All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

Unlike [4D Neural Voxel Splatting](16404-4d-neural-voxel-splatting.md), which may rely on different voxelization strategies, CDF specifically utilizes a Dense Hash Encoding (DHE) multi-hash construction combined with a Hash Feature Decoder to balance storage efficiency and representational capacity [S1].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states that the method (CDF) replaces learnable multi-resolution hash grids with a 'compact neural function' (Hash Feature Decoder) to reduce memory footprint (storage efficiency). It further details the use of 'Dense Hash Encoding' (DHE) with k=128 parallel hash functions to produce signatures and a 'Hash Feature Decoder' consisting of Linear Layers to synthesize features. The text explicitly mentions that this design provides a 'favorable balance between storage efficiency, computational fidelity, and representational capacity' and uses only 4-5 resolution levels compared to typical deeper hierarchies, supporting the claim of balancing these factors.
